findings.text: follow-on: is_raw_receipt decides by filename shape alone, and the job-id it derives from the router's request-receipt rotation is not the marker the module's own docstring claims. The module states a request receipt 'carries no job id at all', which holds for requests.jsonl but not for a date-suffixed rotation. receipts_job_id's pattern (-(\d+)\.jsonl(?:\.\d+)?(?:\.gz)?\Z) reads requests-2026-10-01.jsonl as raw receipt job '01'; reproduced from a scratch copy of the head: is_raw_receipt('requests-2026-10-01.jsonl') is True with job '01', against requests.jsonl which is correctly False. A raw serving receipt and the router's request receipts live in different directories, and the plan states the retention command never opens the directory the request files live in, so the misclassification is reachable today only through a hand-edited or forged manifest naming such a path with an eligible age and digest; recorded because the guard's by-name claim overstates what a shape test proves, and a future placement of request rotations beside the receipts would make the name check the only thing keeping them from the deletion set -- it is not sufficient for that.

follow_ons.text: raw_receipt_files globs *.jsonl, so a rotated or compressed raw receipt (foo-123.jsonl.1, foo-123.jsonl.1.gz) is accepted as a raw file by is_raw_receipt and by the index's discovery regex but is never enumerated for retirement. The module docstring asserts the raw file never rolls, which is what makes this unreachable today; if rotation or gzip of raw receipts is ever added, retirement silently misses them rather than refusing. Not a wrong-direction defect: a missed file is left alone.

The deletion licence is the per-window equality of the three token counters against whichever minute and hour files are on disk, and nothing in the eligibility test distinguishes a tier rebuilt under the current compaction code from a tier compacted before per-leaf counts landed. The plan's rule 2 requires that rebuild first ('Tiers are rebuilt from raw before anything is deleted', 'its rebuilt tiers passed the check in rule 2'), and the plan's own follow-up f-srw-009 records that a pre-per-leaf-counts tier declares no obs.leaves and that the rebuild must happen 'while every raw file is still on disk ... after retention they cannot'. So this command licenses deletion on a figure the rebuild makes meaningful, and must be ordered after that rebuild; the command neither performs nor names that prerequisite. Out of this node's declared scope (the node is the listing-and-apply mechanism, and the rebuild is f-srw-009's stated prerequisite), recorded so the ordering is not lost.

item_verdicts.goal: The node's declared goal is the retention block's rules 3 and 7-of-'+2: a listing pass that judges each raw receipt file eligible only when its serve job is not running, its last parseable row is more than the threshold old, and its minute and hour compactions reproduce its own totals window by window; and an apply pass that deletes exactly a frozen manifest's files, after re-checking each. The commit does this. telemetry_retention.scan judges liveness once for the whole listing (default_running_job_ids, one squeue for the account, and a scheduler that cannot be run raises rather than reading as an empty set), the 24-hour quiet window, the age measured from the last parseable row rather than mtime, and compare_tiers' per-window, per-counter equality over the raw file's own span using TelemetryIndex.partitioned_total on each tier in isolation. write_manifest freezes path, size, sha256 of the file and of both siblings, and last row time; apply_manifest re-checks liveness, quietness, age and all three digests per file and removes only raw receipt files, refusing a compacted tier by name. Every uncertain path fails safe: a missing or unreadable tier, an absent window, a stale tier total, a changed digest, or a manifest entry missing a digest all keep the file. The one gap, the request-receipt rotation the by-name guard does not positively exclude, is recorded as the single finding.
